title: Space and probability preservation under compilation
statement: Let $m,d,k_D,N$ be nonnegative integers, let $[0mA$ be a nondeterministic register machine with $m$ registers and $d$ oracle indices, let $x$ be a bit string, let $	ext{oracle}$ assign a Boolean answer to each oracle index and bit string, and let $D$ be a deterministic Turing machine with $k_D$ work tapes. Suppose the register machine halts after $N$ choice bits on every choice string of length $N$, with every configuration before halting satisfying the guard that each register has binary length at most $W$ and every oracle call is clean and uses at most $B$ work-tape cells per head position. Then there is a time bound $T$ such that the compiled nondeterministic Turing machine halts on every choice string of length $T$, uses at most $m(W+2)+k_D(2B+1)$ work-tape cells on each such run, and accepts within $T$ steps exactly when the register machine can produce result true after $N$ choices. Moreover, for each Boolean value $b$, the fraction of length-$T$ choice strings on which the compiled machine outputs exactly $b$ equals the fraction of length-$N$ choice strings on which the register machine's result is $b$.
